title: The Exterior Derivative and Cartan Calculus

items.title: A graded derivation of the algebra of differential forms
items.strategy: Define the degree convention and its Koszul-sign Leibniz rule on the established graded form algebra.

items.title: The exterior derivative by the invariant vector-field formula
items.strategy: State the alternating Koszul formula locally for smooth vector fields, postponing tensoriality to the next lemma.

items.title: The invariant exterior-derivative formula is $C^\infty$-multilinear
items.strategy: Replace one input by $fX$ and cancel each derivative-of-$f$ term against the Lie-bracket product rule; then use the local tensor criterion for smoothness.

items.title: The exterior derivative is local
items.strategy: Apply the invariant formula to vector fields restricted to a neighbourhood where the two forms agree.

items.title: The exterior derivative of a function is its differential
items.strategy: Specialize the invariant formula to degree zero and identify its value on every vector field with the established differential.

items.title: The local coordinate formula for the exterior derivative
items.strategy: Evaluate the tensorial invariant formula on commuting coordinate fields and obtain $d(\sum_I\omega_I dx^I)=\sum_I d\omega_I\wedge dx^I$.

items.title: The exterior derivative is a graded derivation
items.strategy: Use the coordinate expression on wedge monomials, then invoke locality to pass from a chart to the manifold.

items.title: The exterior derivative squares to zero
items.strategy: In coordinates pair symmetric second derivatives with antisymmetric wedges, and globalize the identity by locality.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the exterior derivative
items.strategy: Combine the preceding construction with the fact that a degree-one graded derivation is determined in a chart by functions and coordinate one-forms.

items.title: The exterior derivative commutes with restriction
items.strategy: Restate locality as equality between the derivative of a restriction and the restriction of the derivative.

items.title: The exterior derivative commutes with pullback
items.strategy: Prove the identity first for functions and coordinate generators, extend by the graded derivation rule, and use locality.

items.title: Pullback carries closed forms to closed forms and exact forms to exact forms
items.strategy: Apply pullback naturality to $d\omega=0$ and to $\omega=d\eta$; the terms closed and exact are used provisionally only.

items.title: The exterior derivative does not enlarge support
items.strategy: Use locality on the open complement of the support, where the form is zero.

items.title: The Lie derivative of a tensor field
items.strategy: Differentiate pullback along a local flow, using the local-diffeomorphism pullback convention for mixed tensors.

items.title: The flow definition of tensor Lie derivative is local and well-defined
items.strategy: Use local uniqueness of integral curves to show two local flows agree near $(0,p)$, hence give the same derivative at zero.

items.title: Tensor Lie derivative agrees with $X$ on functions and bracket on vector fields
items.strategy: Differentiate function pullback and compare the inverse-time pushforward convention with the established vector-field Lie derivative.

items.title: The Lie derivative is a derivation of the tensor algebra
items.strategy: Differentiate the naturality of tensor products and contractions under a local-flow pullback.

items.title: The coordinate formula for the Lie derivative of a covariant tensor
items.strategy: Evaluate the tensor-derivation identity on coordinate vector fields and use $\mathcal L_X\partial_i=[X,\partial_i]$.

items.title: The coordinate formula for the Lie derivative of a contravariant tensor
items.strategy: Apply the tensor-derivation law to a coordinate tensor expansion and differentiate its vector-field factors.

items.title: A tensor field is flow-invariant exactly when its Lie derivative vanishes
items.strategy: Differentiate the pullback curve for one direction and solve the resulting homogeneous derivative equation locally for the converse.

items.title: The Lie derivative of a differential form
items.strategy: Specialize the tensor Lie derivative to alternating covariant tensors.

items.title: Lie derivative of forms is a degree-zero graded derivation
items.strategy: Restrict the tensor product rule to the wedge product of alternating tensors.

items.title: Cartan's magic formula
items.strategy: Check $\mathcal L_X=d\iota_X+\iota_Xd$ on functions and one-forms, then extend because both sides are degree-zero derivations of the form algebra.

items.title: Lie derivative commutes with the exterior derivative
items.strategy: Expand Cartan's formula on both composites and cancel using $d^2=0$.

items.title: Cartan commutator identities
items.strategy: State the graded commutator once and compute it from Cartan's formula, $d^2=0$, and the interior-product antiderivation identities.

items.title: Lie derivatives are natural for related vector fields
items.strategy: Use the invariant form formula together with pullback naturality and the relation of Lie brackets for related fields.

items.title: Differentiation of a pulled-back form along a time-dependent flow
items.strategy: Differentiate the two-time evolution identity and separate variation of the form from infinitesimal pullback by $X_t$.

items.title: A closed form is flow-invariant when its contraction is zero
items.strategy: Cartan's formula vanishes term by term when $d\omega=0$ and $\iota_X\omega=0$, then use the flow-invariance criterion.

items.title: A differential ideal in the algebra of forms
items.strategy: Define a graded wedge ideal stable under the now-established exterior derivative.

items.title: The annihilator ideal of a distribution is frame-independent
items.strategy: Complete each local annihilator frame to a coframe and show both sets generate precisely the forms vanishing on the distribution.

items.title: The Pfaffian Frobenius criterion
items.strategy: Evaluate $d\theta^a$ on tangent fields for necessity, use a local coframe to obtain wedge coefficients for sufficiency, and identify the frame-independent differential ideal.

items.title: The codimension-one Frobenius criterion
items.strategy: In a local coframe beginning with $\alpha$, identify $d\alpha\in(\alpha)$ with $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$.

items.title: Closed constant-rank one-forms define integrable hyperplane fields
items.strategy: A nowhere-zero closed one-form satisfies the codimension-one wedge criterion, yielding integrability of its kernel.

items.title: The exterior derivative is $C^\infty$-linear
items.strategy: Refute the claim with $d(f\omega)=df\wedge\omega+f\,d\omega$ and a nonconstant function.

items.title: The exterior derivative depends on a Riemannian metric
items.strategy: Point to the invariant construction, which uses only smooth functions, vector fields, brackets, and forms.

items.title: Every closed differential form is globally exact
items.strategy: Use the angular one-form on the punctured plane as a direct counterexample; defer its period proof to the integration page.

items.title: Lie derivative and interior product commute for all vector fields
items.strategy: Refute it by $[\mathcal L_X,\iota_Y]=\iota_{[X,Y]}$ for a noncommuting pair.

items.title: $\alpha\wedge d\alpha$ vanishes for every one-form
items.strategy: Use the standard contact form $dz-x\,dy$ on three-space to calculate a nonzero obstruction.

items.title: Pullback of a compactly supported form is always compactly supported
items.strategy: Use a constant nonproper map into the support of a compactly supported form to produce noncompact pullback support.

title: The Exterior Derivative and Cartan Calculus — Examples

items.title: Exterior derivatives of coordinate one-forms
items.strategy: Apply the coordinate formula to $dx^i=d(x^i)$ and use $d^2=0$.

items.title: The Euclidean area form is closed
items.strategy: Compute $d(dx\wedge dy)$ from the coordinate formula.

items.title: The angular one-form on the punctured plane is closed
items.strategy: Differentiate the explicit rational-coordinate angular form and cancel its two-form coefficient.

items.title: The angular one-form has no global potential
items.strategy: Record local angle primitives; defer the nonexistence proof to its nonzero unit-circle period on the later integration page.

items.title: Curl and divergence encoded by the exterior derivative
items.strategy: Compute $d$ on Euclidean one- and two-form coordinate expressions without a metric-free vector-field identification.

items.title: Lie derivative of the Euclidean metric under dilations
items.strategy: Insert the radial dilation field in the covariant-tensor coordinate formula for the Euclidean metric.

items.title: Lie derivative of an area form and planar divergence
items.strategy: Use Cartan's formula on $dx\wedge dy$ and identify the remaining coefficient with coordinate divergence.

items.title: Cartan's formula for a coordinate vector field
items.strategy: Evaluate both terms in Cartan's formula on a coordinate expression for a differential form.

items.title: A contact form on three-space
items.strategy: For $\alpha=dz-x\,dy$, calculate $\alpha\wedge d\alpha\ne0$ and invoke the codimension-one obstruction.

items.title: An integrable Pfaffian equation with a local first integral
items.strategy: Exhibit a nowhere-zero defining form satisfying the Pfaffian criterion and write a local first integral for its kernel.

items.title: A nonproper pullback destroys compact support
items.strategy: Pull a compactly supported form back by a constant map whose image lies in its nonzero region, so the pullback has noncompact support.

items.title: Time-dependent pullback differentiation for a translation
items.strategy: Write the two-time translation evolution and verify $\dot\omega_t+\mathcal L_{X_t}\omega_t$ term by term.
